correctness.rationale: The spanning-path characterization follows from disjoint chains of nilpotent partial bijections; induced-subgraph isomorphism is equivalent to shift-invariant adjacency; least repeated clique-label distance forces a primitive-period word with one component per residue. originality.rationale: The primary arXiv:2303.12387 addresses abstract monogenic inverse-monoid isomorphism types, arXiv:1809.04422 characterizes inverse monoids of graph partial automorphisms, and arXiv:2112.14371 Proposition 2.3 establishes related Toeplitz residue decomposition. Explicitly excluding those prior components, the new graph-restricted maximal-index count and sharp cluster-size criterion are not implied by inspected published statements. Broader partition-preserving inverse-monoid coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: The Toeplitz graph residue-class mechanism itself is classical (explicit in arXiv:2112.14371, Proposition 2.3); it is not independently novel.
An equivalent extremizer formula may exist in wider literature on partial permutations preserving equivalence relations or complementary multipartite graphs, beyond the inspected sources.

value.rationale: The largest possible nilpotency index is intrinsic to a finite inverse monoid and its maximal-index elements are natural extremizers. Sharp balance of clique component sizes supplies an informative nonexistence boundary; exact labeled multiplicity distinguishes uniform and almost-uniform partitions across every finite size. The statement bridges partial automorphism semigroups with Toeplitz graph labeling and applies to equivalence relations and complements.
